passages.provision_quote: Allows the general assembly to amend congressional districts at a time other than the first regular session of the general assembly convening immediately following the United States decennial census.
passages.note: Engrossed bill text/digest; shows the general assembly redrawing congressional districts directly and restricting judicial challenges, predating the Senate floor vote.
Bill overview page records the Senate defeated HB 1032 on third reading by Roll Call 8, 19 yeas to 31 nays, but does not list individual votes.
Senate Roll Call 8 lists Bray's surname among the 31 Nay votes on HB 1032's third reading, which the Senate defeated.

rows.reasoning: The only evidence is Sen. Bray's Nay vote in Senate Roll Call 8, which defeated HB 1032 on third reading 19-31; the bill would have let 'the general assembly...amend congressional districts' outside the normal post-census session while limiting judicial challenges to the new map. A No vote on this single bill rules out support for enacting that particular legislature-drawn map and procedure but does not show whether Bray instead favors 'independent citizens' commissions,' 'independent redistricting commissions with equal representation from both major parties,' 'bipartisan legislative committees with strict rules requiring supermajority approval,' or just a different version of legislature-drawn maps, so no rung is established.
